finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: user-supplied POST 'feed' is passed to file_get_contents with no scheme, host, or IP validation and no auth check. Blind (only strlen returned), but reaches internal hosts and link-local metadata endpoints, and file:// enables a length-based local file probe.

trace.note: Branch entered on POST with isset($_POST['feed']); no require_admin() call
Raw attacker value passed to file_get_contents (allow_url_fopen default on)

finding.guards_checked: None. No authentication/authorization, no scheme allowlist (http, https, ftp, file all pass), no host/IP block for loopback/RFC1918/link-local, no redirect re-validation, no timeout or size limit.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 checks only REQUEST_METHOD and isset($_POST['feed']); the feed value reaches file_get_contents at import.php:12 unvalidated, with no require_admin() call (that only guards the set_webhook branch at line 18). The directory contains only import.php, so there is no shared prepend, middleware, or helper that adds a guard.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: import.php:11 gates on POST and isset($_POST['feed']) with no auth, import.php:12 passes the raw value to file_get_contents, and import.php:13 echoes only strlen($xml); no scheme, host, or IP validation exists anywhere on the path, so the unauthenticated SSRF is real.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: admin-supplied 'set_webhook' is passed to curl_init and executed with curl_exec; response discarded. Requires an admin session.
finding.sink: curl_init() at import.php:20 and curl_exec() at import.php:22

trace.note: curl_exec runs the request; RETURNTRANSFER set and output not echoed (blind)

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check only (non-empty is_admin, lines 4-9 and 18). Its assignment is outside this file, so its strength is unverified. No scheme, host, or IP validation. CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS not set, so accepted schemes depend on the libcurl build.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9, called at import.php:18. It checks only that $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty, which is an authorization gate, not URL validation. No scheme, host, or IP check exists between lines 19 and 20.
verdict.reason: The sink at import.php:20 is reachable only past require_admin() (import.php:18, exits 403 without a non-empty $_SESSION['is_admin'] per lines 5-8), so the value at line 19 is set by an admin-only caller rather than an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, failing the source requirement. The trace lines themselves are accurate, and the candidate's own text states that it requires an admin session.
